what_happened: The job to give OLY-A-07 a mechanism, a spec-and-vocabulary owner check (a "requirements engineer" in hestia.rs), was rejected at the final verdict. The verifier gave three major findings and no blockers. No acceptance criteria or checks are listed as failed. (1) The spec measure says `athena status` shows things that its `requirement` line does not show. (2) The new requirements engineer copies existing rules, and its two new rules can never fire on main because CI already enforces them. (3) The accepted reading misstated the request, so passing criteria do not show the request was met.
cause: Nothing cross-checked the accepted reading against the request's wording, or the new check and its measure text against what the code and CI already do, before the verifier's final verdict. The reading was accepted although it misstated the request. The built check duplicates CI enforcement, so it cannot fire. The recorded measure describes status output the code does not produce. A new measure or rule was never replayed against real main or real status output to show it can fire or that its text is true.
other_causes: The producer wrote the measure text for docs/spec.toml without comparing it with what status.rs actually prints.
Nothing required a new rule to be shown to fail on a known-bad input and pass on main, so a rule that duplicates CI went unnoticed.
open_hypotheses: The fields do not show which part of the request the reading misstated, so it is unclear whether the reading or the producer introduced the duplicate rules.
It is unknown whether the request itself named rules already enforced by CI.
prevention: Add a check before the producer runs that compares the accepted reading with the request's own wording. Require any new rule or check, and any measure text claiming what status shows, to be shown on real data: the rule must fail on a known-bad input and pass on current main, and it must not duplicate a rule CI already enforces. Check the measure's claims about status output against the real output. Gate counts show 0 disagreements for every gate, so no gate is a candidate to relax or remove.
proposed_request: Give OLY-A-07 a mechanism: a spec-and-vocabulary owner check. Outcomes: (1) A check in hestia.rs flags a spec-or-vocabulary violation that nothing in CI already catches. For each rule, show one known-bad input that it flags and show that it passes on current main. Do not add a rule that CI already enforces. (2) The OLY-A-07 measure text in docs/spec.toml says only what `athena status` really shows, and each claim is checked against the actual status output. (3) Acceptance criteria quote the request's wording and each cites a command that ran. Include the CHANGELOG.md entry and run cargo fmt --check, clippy --all-targets -D warnings and the full cargo test, including the athena-cli tests that read status output.
